title: DataPulse MY historical-observation/v1 envelope
description: Contract for one filed historical observation of an upstream dataset. The envelope records what was requested, what was actually captured, how it was normalised, and what a consumer may conclude. It deliberately cannot express freshness or authority claims; those live on separate axes.

observation_id.description: Stable identifier of this observation, unique across all datasets and cycles.

dataset_id.description: Identifier of the observed dataset in the DataPulse manifest.

source_identity.description: Who the source says it is, or who independent evidence supports. Never a certification of authority.

limitation.const: Identity is declared or independently supported; it is not a certification of authority, control, or authenticity.

source_url.description: Canonical catalogue URL of the dataset.

observed_request_url.description: The exact URL DataPulse actually requested. May differ from source_url after redirects or mirror selection.

observed_at.description: Instant DataPulse filed this observation (digests computed, envelope sealed). This is the DataPulse observation time; it is neither the retrieval time nor the source content date.

retrieved_at.description: Instant the source request completed. Null when no completed request exists. Kept separate from observed_at and from source_content_date.

source_content_date.description: Date the content itself claims to be about (its vintage), extracted from the content or its headers. Null when not extractable. Never inferred from retrieval or observation time.

source_version.description: Upstream version identifier for the observed content. Either the explicit unknown marker, or a value with an auditable basis. A bare string other than 'unknown' is rejected: when the version is not known, 'unknown' is the only permitted bare value, so fabricated versions cannot be smuggled through this member.

capture_policy.description: What the pipeline intended to retain for this dataset.

capture_status.description: What was actually retained. Only 'captured' means the defined source bytes are held in full; 'partial' (for example a truncated transfer) is not captured.

source_digest.description: SHA-256 over exactly the source bytes that were captured. Asserted ONLY when capture_status is 'captured'; must be null for partial, metadata-only, failed, or absent captures.

observation_digest.description: Domain-separated digest over the canonical form of this envelope (excluding observation_digest itself). The cycle_root commitment is computed over these digests.

shape_fingerprint.description: Value-insensitive structural fingerprint of the content (keys, types, headers). Null when the format exposes no defensible structural evidence.

limitation.const: Structural fingerprint over keys, types, and headers only; it is not a digest of the source content.

normalized_projection.description: Whether a normalised projection of the capture is retained, in what format, and with what known record count.

normalization_profile_version.description: Version of the normalisation rules that produced the projection. Two projections are comparable only under the same version.

previous_observation_id.description: Identifier of the immediately preceding observation OF THE SAME dataset. Null for a dataset's first observation.

previous_observation_digest.description: Digest of the immediately preceding observation OF THE SAME dataset. This is same-dataset history; it is NEVER the attestation chain head (.attestations/chain_head.json) or any other aggregate commitment. Domain-separated so chain-head values (bare hex in the attestation plane) cannot be pasted here.

change_from_previous.description: Comparison against the previous same-dataset observation. 'incomparable' means the two normalisations could not be aligned (for example different normalization_profile_version).

verification.description: Cryptographic verification state of this observation. A separate axis from health/freshness classification; the two must not be conflated.

method.description: How verification was or would be performed, for example digest recomputation plus attestation-chain signature check.

limitation.const: Verification status is cryptographic and procedural only; it is neither a freshness classification nor a statement of semantic truth.

attestation_ref.description: Reference to the attestation-plane entry covering the cycle this observation belongs to. An aggregate-plane reference; it does not replace same-dataset history.

witness_refs.description: References to independent corroborating records (transparency-log entries, third-party snapshots). Empty when no witness exists.

claim_boundary.description: Per-observation statement of what may and may not be concluded. Both lists must be non-empty: there is always at least one valid conclusion and at least one boundary.

unknown_reasons.description: Members whose values are explicitly unknown in this observation. Closed vocabulary; a reason may only name a member that can actually be unknown. When source_version is 'unknown', 'source_version' must appear here.

cycle_root.description: Merkle-style commitment over all observation digests retained in one cycle. Lets a third party verify a single observation against one root without holding the full set.

contract_digest.description: Digest over the pinned source of the code that produced this observation. An observation's validity is bound to this digest: a material change to the producing code invalidates prior verifications instead of letting them persist silently.

superseded_by.description: Observation that replaces this one in the same dataset's history. Null while this observation is current.

invalidated_by.description: What invalidated this observation: a successor observation id, or the contract digest of the material code change that broke it. Null while the observation stands.

declared.description: What the source or contract declares, each entry with its basis. Never inferred from observed.

observed.description: What DataPulse actually observed, each entry with its basis. Never inferred from declared.

publisher_credential.description: Reserved for a standards-shaped publisher credential. MUST be null in this phase; populating it requires a schema contract change, not a producer decision.

verifier_credential.description: Reserved for a standards-shaped verifier credential. MUST be null in this phase; populating it requires a schema contract change, not a producer decision.

replay_state.description: Whether, and how far, the source content can be reconstructed from what this observation retains. A separate axis from the ten health statuses: a fresh health status does not imply replayable, and a replayable capture does not imply semantic truth.
